Two figures in white marble beside the classical fluted column: Ares, god of war, and his son Deimoz. Ares is the larger, disciplined and calm, the red team who proves a flaw and mends it. He wears a crested war helmet. His spear stands UPRIGHT and grounded: the wooden butt rests on the floor, the shaft rises vertically at his side, the bronze spearhead points UP toward the sky. The spear is never inverted and the blade never points down. His round hoplon shield is held on his forearm or rests upright against his leg on the ground; it never floats in the air. Beside him stands Deimoz, his son, a younger warrior in a plain helmet, the dread that rides into every battle with his father; Deimoz is the one who drives the attack, one hand extended toward a small marble tablet that stands for the code under test. From the shield and from Deimoz's hand, fine threads flow toward the tablet: clear signal-red threads that GLOW with a soft luminous halo, like gentle magic, carrying the proven finding into the open; a few muted-gold threads, also faintly glowing, stay held close. On the shield face one glowing line runs from a red circle to a green circle, a flaw proven and closed, red turning to green, proof not blood. Owner-authorized family exception: Ares and Deimoz use luminous signal red where the Pantheon family uses sky blue for flow, because together they are the red team. Warm ivory background, white marble, soft daylight from the upper left, gentle long shadows, generous empty space, calm and exact. The only glow in the frame is the fine magical halo along the threads; everything else stays clean daylight marble. No dark background, no fire, no spilled blood, no chariot, no fallen bodies, no neon signage, no smoky cinematic lighting. No readable text.
